citations.review_text: please dont make the mistake of getting this game. i have wanted this game for about 2 years and every time its gone on sale, i have been very close to buying it. i decided to give in to the urges today and finally try to have a great time on this game that ive heard so many good things about. The game takes 45 minutes to load in to a server which was pretty annoying but i thought it was just because it was my first time playing. i join a server and immediately die to a bear while breaking a tree. whatever, i thought, at least i havent met an annoying player yet. next respawn im walking over to a tree while i get shot in the head with a pistol. i then respawned one more time and proceeded to get slammed in the head by a bolt action from a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ on an oil rig 5 kilometers away from me. so thats that. please dont ever get this game its not worth it and ive never disliked a game more than this one.

Massively multiplayer first-person survival game.  You have been dropped into a hostile world, naked and without equipment.  Learn how to gather materials and craft them into usable gear.  Survive against hostile wildlife and fellow players.  Make a place for yourself.

I do not begrudge people for liking this game.  I do not, for various reasons.

To begin with, the game is a pig on my machine, and my machine has been able to run just about anything I've thrown at it, and in most cases streamed it live at the same time.  When it took fifteen minutes or so to load the game, someone in my stream suggested my machine couldn't handle Rust.  I showed them my specs.  They admitted it could.

Loading the game a second time offstream also took fifteen minutes, so whatever the hell it was doing the first time wasn't just initializing, or wasn't only that.  This feels like the antithesis of a fat-client system.  In my mind it doesn't lend itself to impulse play...it suggests you need to start the game, then go grab dinner or something before settling in to do as many hours as you can in a session so you don't need to load it again.

I did the tutorial.  I got a Steam achievement for completing it...apparently a lot of people don't.  Got through the basics, took a while to understand some fundamental concepts (and the small font didn't help with that - fogey alert) but I managed.  Only died twice.  Did the missions provided by the trainer, geared myself up, clothed myself, got into a little boat and set off toward the main island.

And got ganked.  Not by players, but by NPCs in boats that surrounded mine.  I then woke up, naked and unequipped, in a starting area.  This tells me ganking isn't something that evolved amongst the player base, not something that one person did, and then another, and then everyone does.  This is an integral part of the game.  It's built into the tutorial.

And that's not my flavor of fun.  For those people who do find that fun, for those who wish …

citations.review_text: I cant boot the game because me pc is trash but Im not gonna refund it because in the future I will maybe prob eventually get a good pc also I have 7 hours in loading screens

[h1] Rust has the worst introduction of any game I have ever played. [/h1]

First off, as soon as you load the game and look for servers, you are met with a server list full of premium servers, like the game can't detect whether you have premium or not. Just an annoying way to advertise your premium service, a small but constant inconvenience because you have to reapply your filters every time.

Second, the loading times for entering a new server are not great. If you want to join and leave servers quickly, you're gonna be spending half an hour just cycling between a couple servers. Now if you are not made to feel like you have to cycle servers, the loading time wouldn't really be that bad. This is going to be relevant in point three.

Third, where is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stone? Seriously, The tutorial tells you to gather stone, but there is none. There are thousands of rocks and boulders, but for whatever un-immersive reason, you can't mine them. The stone nodes in Rust are rarer than diamonds in Minecraft. My friends tried to say that this is just Rust's infamously, "brutally hard" start. I reject that statement. If a player is running around for hours looking for something, that's not brutally hard. That's brutally boring. 

Fourth, every server is so old. It is hard to find a server that is just a few hours old. That said, I did find one. Thought I'd find stone there, and I did, and immediately starved to death because I'd been looking for it for a ridiculous amount of time. 

Fifth, every region outside the U.S is just everyone speaking Russian. Nothing wrong with that, but more narrowed regional matchmaking can help players join servers with people they can talk to. After all, Rust is famous for its multiplayer. 

All in all, if every new player is going to have this abysmal of a time trying to get into the very basics of the game, Rust is not going to grow. It already seems highly tailored to its old player-base, as everyone you meet has 80 trillion hours. The audienc…

claims.claim: Reviewers complain about encountering cheaters or players using recoil scripts during matches.

citations.review_text: Great game if you ever wanted to spend 8 hours farming rocks just to get raided by a guy named xX_SleepDeprived_420_Xx who has been online for 36 hours straight. Half the servers are people with recoil scripts, the other half are people pretending they don't have recoil scripts.

I was disappointed after encountering dozens of cheaters and seeing the lag issues. Throw in the Russian kids waiting on the beach just to kill you with a rock for the fun of it, and the game simply isn't in a playable state right now. Still, the maps and game mechanics are excellent tho but need to fix those things for playable game.

I will change it to a positive recommendation once the issues are resolved. Sadly not recommending now.

claims.claim: Players face performance issues and frame rate drops on high population servers.

citations.review_text: Best Game Ever, played  for more than 4k hours now i still can't hate it , however i have a decent pc with RTX 5060, I5 14th Gen, 32 GB Ram and i still struggle with FPS in High pop Servers, The Game Lack serious optimisations !

**⭐☆☆☆☆ (1/5)**

I've put way too many hours into Rust hoping it would get better, but instead it's just become one of the most frustrating games I've ever played.

The biggest issue is the **cheaters**. No matter what server you join, it feels like there's always someone using ESP, aimbots, recoil scripts, or other cheats. You spend hours farming resources, building a base, and getting geared, only to get wiped by someone who somehow knows exactly where you are. It completely ruins the survival experience and makes every death feel suspicious instead of deserved.

Then there's the community. While there are some good players, a huge portion of the player base is unbelievably toxic. Constant trash talk, griefing, door camping, roof camping, offline raiding, and players who only seem interested in making everyone else's experience miserable. New players barely stand a chance.

The grind is another massive problem. You can spend an entire day gathering materials, crafting, and expanding your base, only to log in the next morning and find everything gone because your base was raided while you were offline. Losing progress is part of Rust, but when it happens over and over, it starts to feel like you're wasting your time.

Performance is also disappointing. Even on decent PCs, the game can suffer from poor optimization, random frame drops, stuttering, long loading times, and crashes. Every major update seems to introduce new bugs while old issues remain.

The learning curve is brutal. Beginners are thrown into the game with almost no guidance, and experienced players dominate every server. Unless you already have hundreds or thousands of hours, expect to spend most of your time dying.

The game also demands an unhealthy amount of time. If you don't play every day, someone else will out-farm you, out-progress you, and eventually destroy everything you've built. It often feels less like a game and more like a second job.

Overall, Rust has an incredible concept, but the c…

My cousin and I had become fairly invested in Rust, spending hours building up our base and enjoying the challenge the game offers. That experience came to an abrupt halt when we ran into a player using cheats. He eliminated both of us instantly, took over our base, and continued to kill us repeatedly from across the map with no way for us to fight back or even understand what was happening in real time. It became clear in that moment that there was little point in continuing.

After that encounter, we learned that this kind of cheating is a widespread and ongoing issue within the Rust community, not an isolated incident. Knowing that this could happen again at any time made it difficult to justify investing further time into the game.

I wanted to like Rust, and in many ways I did. The foundation is there for a genuinely excellent survival experience. However, if fair play and a level playing field matter to you, this is worth strong consideration before committing your time. If hacking and cheating are not deal breakers for you, the game may still be worth playing.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe base building as a core mechanic, allowing players to progress from simple wooden shacks to defended fortresses using complex elements like electricity and piping.

citations.review_text: Absolutely the best open-world survival game. The mechanics of movement/flight and interfaces are very comfortable. Building, electrical using their own rust watts(rW), industrial loot moving piping, farming with plant genetics. The possibilities on this game are endless.. I'm a strict solo. Only played with a team for a short period of time being their builder.

**Rust** is one of the most exciting and challenging survival games I have ever played. Every time you join a new server, you start with nothing and must gather resources, build a base, craft equipment, and survive against both the environment and other players. Because every server and every wipe is different, no two experiences ever feel the same.

What I enjoy the most is the freedom the game offers. You can choose to play solo, team up with friends, trade with other players, or become a powerful clan that dominates the server. There are countless ways to play, and every decision can completely change your experience. Playing with friends is especially fun, as building a base, defending against raids, and exploring monuments together creates unforgettable moments.

The building system is one of Rust's strongest features. Watching a small wooden shelter grow into a heavily defended fortress is incredibly satisfying. The crafting system is also deep, allowing players to gradually unlock better equipment and weapons as they progress. Combined with the large open world and constant player interaction, the game always feels fresh and unpredictable.

If I had to mention a downside, it would be the steep learning curve. New players can easily lose everything after being killed or raided, which can be frustrating. Some servers may also have cheaters or highly experienced players that make survival difficult for beginners. However, finding a well-managed server greatly improves the overall experience.

Overall, Rust is an outstanding survival game with excellent base building, PvP combat, exploration, and multiplayer gameplay. Although it can be unforgiving at times, the satisfaction of successfully defending your base, winning raids, or surviving an entire wipe makes every challenge worthwhile. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys survival games and competitive multiplayer experiences.

Ein absolut erstklassiges Survival Spiel. Die Atmosphäre ist stimmungsvoll, das Gameplay sorgt durchgehend für Nervenkitzel und die Fights sind an Intensität kaum zu überbieten. Vor allem im Team entfaltet das Spiel sein volles Potenzial und sorgt für unvergessliche Sessions. Der Basebau ist angenehm komplex und erfordert echtes technisches Verständnis. Man merkt einfach, wie viel Arbeit in die stetige und gelungene Weiterentwicklung gesteckt wird.
